title: Fourth-moment bound for independent sums
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and for each coordinate $i$ let $\Omega_i$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $p_i$ and a real-valued function $X_i$. Suppose each $X_i$ has mean zero and third moment zero, and satisfies $\mathbb E[X_i^4]\le3(\mathbb E[X_i^2])^2$. Let $a_S$ be real coefficients indexed by subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with $a_S=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. Then the multilinear polynomial $\sum_S a_S\prod_{i\in S}X_i$, evaluated on independent samples from the $p_i$, satisfies $\mathbb E[Y^4]\le3(\mathbb E[Y^2])^2$.
hypotheses_covered: each coordinate has a probability mass function $p_i$
each coordinate has a real-valued random variable $X_i$
each $X_i$ satisfies the stated fourth-moment bound
the coefficient family is indexed by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$
coefficients vanish for subsets of size greater than $1$
